overall_summary: Bitcoin is holding near sixty-four thousand as traders wait on today's critical CPI print, keeping the tape in a clear risk-off hold. Crypto has mixed catalysts with SEC regulation talks and Fidelity ether staking support offset by miner selling and a Harmony exploit. Softer yields and small-business optimism help, but Middle East tensions and Fed political noise cap conviction until inflation data lands.
key_points: Markets brace for today's pivotal US CPI print
SEC Aug 14 meeting eyes crypto regulation proposal
Fidelity adds staking to nearly $900M ether ETF
Yields ease; Red Sea and Hormuz risks linger

items.title: Bitcoin Holds Near $64K Ahead of Critical US CPI Print
items.summary: Bitcoin is stuck in a tight range around sixty-three to sixty-four thousand dollars with volatility crushed to multi-year lows. Traders are bracing for today's July CPI data, expected to show headline inflation easing to about three point four percent. A soft print could ease rate-hike fears and spark a breakout, while a hot one risks more pressure. This is the clearest near-term catalyst that could finally resolve the multi-week stalemate.
items.impact: Binary catalyst likely to drive the next directional move in BTC

items.title: SEC Schedules Aug 14 Meeting to Propose Regulation Crypto
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission will hold an open meeting this Friday to propose its first major formal crypto rulemaking, called Regulation Crypto. It aims to create a tailored offering regime for certain digital asset investment contracts, giving startups a clearer legal path to raise capital. This comes after the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act before recess. Traders should care because durable rules reduce regulatory overhang and could unlock more institutional participation.
items.impact: Positive regulatory clarity catalyst for broader crypto markets

items.title: Harmony Exploit Mints 4 Billion ONE Tokens, Price Crashes 40%
items.summary: An apparent attacker minted roughly four billion unauthorized ONE tokens, equal to more than a quarter of the existing supply, sending the token down about forty percent. Harmony is working with exchanges to freeze funds, rolling out a patch, and considering a blockchain rollback. This is the latest major security incident on a layer-one chain and rattles broader altcoin sentiment. Traders should watch for contagion risk and any spillover selling into majors.
items.impact: Negative for altcoin risk appetite and crypto security perception

items.title: Metaplanet Moves 3,881 BTC Internally Amid $1.4B Paper Loss
items.summary: Japan's Metaplanet transferred three thousand eight hundred eighty-one bitcoin worth about two hundred forty-seven million dollars between wallets it controls. On-chain data shows no deposit to exchanges, so this is not a sale despite the firm sitting on roughly one point four billion dollars in unrealized losses. Large treasury moves like this often spark sell rumors and temporary volatility. Watch the destination wallets closely for any follow-through distribution.
items.impact: Temporary sentiment pressure but no confirmed new supply

items.title: Public Miners Sold $1.78 Billion of Bitcoin This Year
items.summary: Publicly listed bitcoin miners have reduced holdings by about twenty-eight thousand BTC, injecting roughly one point seven eight billion dollars of selling pressure into the market. This has been an underappreciated source of supply alongside ETF outflows and treasury sales. Many miners are pivoting toward AI compute as production costs sit above current prices. The selling helps explain bitcoin's weak year-to-date performance and could ease if remaining miners benefit from lower difficulty.
items.impact: Ongoing marginal supply pressure capping upside

items.title: Fidelity to Add Staking and Payouts to Nearly $900M Ether ETF
items.summary: Fidelity is amending its Ethereum Fund to enable staking of up to one hundred percent of holdings and quarterly cash distributions from rewards. The fund would keep eighty-five percent of gross staking rewards after service fees. This follows similar moves by other issuers and an IRS safe harbor. It makes the product more competitive and attractive to yield-seeking institutions, supporting ether demand and broader crypto ETF innovation.
items.impact: Supportive for ETH and institutional crypto product adoption

items.title: July CPI Due Today: Markets Brace for Inflation Print
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases July Consumer Price Index data at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. Economists expect headline CPI up 0.1 percent month-over-month and 3.4 percent year-over-year, with core at plus 0.2 percent and 2.5 percent. After last week's surprise jobs decline and June's unexpected drop, a cool print could further cut odds of a September Fed hike under Chair Kevin Warsh, while a hot one would revive tightening fears. Crypto and risk assets will react sharply to any surprise on the path of rates and the dollar.
items.impact: High volatility catalyst for BTC, yields, DXY and equities on the print

items.title: 10-Year Yield Eases to Near 4.67% Ahead of CPI
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield slipped toward 4.67-4.68 percent as investors positioned for today's inflation data after earlier climbs driven by oil and hike speculation. Softer energy prices and diplomatic noise around the Middle East helped cool some pressure. For traders, lower yields ease financial conditions and historically support Bitcoin and growth assets if the move holds post-CPI.
items.impact: Easier financial conditions supportive for risk assets if sustained

items.title: Trump Renews Push to Oust Fed Governor Lisa Cook
items.summary: The White House has revived efforts to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over disputed mortgage fraud allegations, sending a letter giving her time to respond. This follows a prior Supreme Court setback protecting Fed independence. Markets watch closely because any successful political pressure on the Board could raise long-term inflation risk premiums, push yields higher, and weaken confidence in the dollar and policy stability.
items.impact: Threat to Fed independence could lift term premiums and volatility

items.title: NFIB Small Business Optimism Jumps to 99.8
items.summary: The NFIB Small Business Optimism Index rose 2.4 points in July to 99.8, beating forecasts near 97 and hitting the highest level in nearly a year. Hiring plans surged and price-increase intentions eased. This points to residual economic resilience even after the weak July payrolls number, which could keep the Fed cautious about cutting too soon but also supports growth narratives for equities and crypto risk appetite.
items.impact: Signals underlying strength that may limit dovish Fed shifts

items.title: Existing Home Sales Slip Slightly in July
items.summary: Existing-home sales fell about 1.7 percent in July to a 4.06 million annualized rate, roughly in line with expectations after prior declines. Inventory tightened a bit and median prices edged higher year-over-year amid still-elevated mortgage rates near 6.8 percent. Housing remains a drag, but the data is not collapsing, so it is unlikely to force an immediate Fed pivot on its own while inflation stays elevated.
items.impact: Mild growth headwind but limited near-term market shock

items.title: Dollar Steady Near 99.8 as Futures Await Inflation Data
items.summary: The US Dollar Index hovered around 99.8 to 99.85 with stock futures mixed to modestly higher, led by Nasdaq strength on AI-related earnings. Markets are in wait-and-see mode after last week's payrolls drop and before CPI and Thursday's PPI. A softer inflation number would likely pressure the dollar and yields further, which is typically constructive for Bitcoin, while anything sticky keeps the greenback bid and risk assets on the defensive.
items.impact: Range-bound DXY until CPI resolves Fed path bets

items.title: US Fires on Ship Breaking Iran Blockade as Hormuz Deal Falters
items.summary: US forces fired Hellfire missiles from a helicopter at a Panama-flagged container ship trying to run the naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Gulf of Oman. At the same time Trump hardened his stance, demanding reparations from Iran, while Pakistan's defense minister still claims a deal on the Strait of Hormuz is close. Shipping traffic has dropped sharply. Traders should care because this waterway handles a huge share of global oil; prolonged disruption or fresh escalation keeps energy prices elevated and risk appetite suppressed.
items.impact: Higher oil prices and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: Houthis Kill Six in Deadly Missile Strike on Red Sea Ship
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels fired ballistic missiles at a commercial vessel in the Bab el-Mandeb strait, killing at least six people including crew members. Yemeni authorities confirmed the attack and it marks one of the deadliest recent hits on shipping. This comes amid the broader Iran conflict. Crypto traders should watch because renewed Red Sea threats force more vessel rerouting around Africa, raising freight costs, delaying supply chains, and adding another layer of energy and inflation risk.
items.impact: Elevated shipping costs and broader Middle East risk premium

items.title: Ukraine Drone Strike Hits Russian Oil Refinery, Kills 13
items.summary: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the TANECO oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, deep inside Russia, killing at least 13 people including a child and wounding dozens more. Ukraine confirmed targeting the facility and a fire was reported. This continues Kyiv's campaign against Russian energy infrastructure. For markets it matters because hits on refining capacity tighten global product supplies and keep pressure on Russian revenues even as broader energy markets stay volatile from the Middle East.
items.impact: Potential support for oil products prices; limited broad risk-asset move

items.title: Colombia 7.4 Quake Death Toll Tops 250, National Emergency
items.summary: A powerful magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia, killing more than 250 people with thousands still missing or injured and widespread damage to buildings and infrastructure. The new president declared a national state of emergency as rescue efforts continue. While primarily a humanitarian disaster, large quakes can briefly hit regional risk sentiment and insurance markets. Traders note any secondary effects on Latin American assets or commodity logistics, though direct global market impact looks limited so far.
items.impact: Localized risk; minor potential drag on regional sentiment

items.title: Hungary Elects New President in Post-Orban Power Shift
items.summary: Hungary's parliament elected former Supreme Court head András Baka as president with a supermajority from the ruling Tisza party. It is a symbolic step by Prime Minister Péter Magyar to dismantle remaining structures from Viktor Orbán's long rule. Fidesz boycotted the vote. European political shifts like this can influence EU cohesion, rule-of-law debates, and ultimately the euro and risk assets if they signal broader alignment changes with Brussels or NATO.
items.impact: Potential longer-term positive for EU stability perception

items.title: Syria Sentences Bashar al-Assad to Death in Absentia
items.summary: A Damascus criminal court sentenced deposed Syrian president Bashar al-Assad and his brother to death in absentia for premeditated murder and crimes against humanity. International arrest warrants were issued. Assad remains in Russia. This is a landmark accountability move after his 2024 ouster. For markets it is mostly symbolic but reinforces the post-Assad transition narrative in the Middle East and could affect regional stability calculations alongside the Iran conflict.
items.impact: Limited direct market effect; symbolic regional political signal
